Subject: Degradation on inference route — request for apportionment

Irene,

Impact looked intermittent but meaningful: about 12% of requests retried, and a handful of client-side timeouts. We logged customer incidents and this is affecting Skyline feature rollout.

Can you confirm how Redwood will calculate uptime for that period? Attached: svc_incident_log_20261129.csv (our front-end traces).

What we need from Redwood:
- start/end times you will count as degraded for our contract
- whether you consider the event a third-party exclusion or eligible for credit
- next steps / timeline for a final determination

Thanks — appreciate a quick acknowledgement and then we can provide more traces if helpful.

— Theo

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:16:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: initial apportionment calc for Skyline incident

Internal — I mapped the Skyline traces to our ingress logs. Preliminary observations:
- Region: us-west-2 endpoints, affected between 01:03:48–01:41:22 UTC (approx).
- Observed two classes of failures: increased token-latency for long sequences (~95p up by 220ms) and a spike in 503s concentrated on a small set of host proxies.
- Proxy-level logs show upstream TCP resets to 10.4.12.0/24 (ProxyNet) during a 37-minute overlap; outside that, there were short-lived latency blips from our autoscaling warm-up (6–8 minutes) that we treat as internal transient.

I attached a workbook with the breakdown and suggested apportionment (time-based):
- Total impact window we’ll count: 38 minutes (01:03:48–01:41:22 UTC)
- Exclude 6 minutes considered internal autoscaling transient
- Of the remaining 32 minutes, 21 minutes correlate to upstream resets from ProxyNet; 11 minutes correlate to degraded CPU scheduling on our serving hosts.

Suggested approach: apportion credits pro-rata: 65% Redwood responsibility, 35% third-party. If legal ops wants full exclusion for ProxyNet, we’ll need vendor confirmation and timeline.

Attachment: sla_apportionment_calc.xlsx (Excel, 72KB)

— Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

- EdgeProxy: please confirm within 72 hours and attach any vendor notices.

EdgeProxy position: given the breadth of the upstream event and the timing alignment, we are requesting that Redwood treat this as a third-party exclusion per section 4.2 of the SLA. Please let us know what additional evidence you need from us.

EdgeProxy Customer Ops
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Theo Martin <theo.martin@skyline.ai>, EdgeProxy Support <support@edgeproxy.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Final determination: partial credit granted (apportionment)

All — thanks for the quick investigation and for the ProxyNet bulletin. After reviewing the evidence (Skyline traces, our ingress logs, proxy telemetry, and ProxyNet notice), Redwood’s determination:

- We will grant a partial SLA credit to Skyline. Rationale: while a substantial portion of the degradation coincides with an upstream ProxyNet incident, our logs show a non-trivial period (approx. 11 minutes) of degraded performance traceable to internal serving host scheduling during the same window. Per the SLA, only the portion attributable to Redwood is credit-eligible.

- Credit apportionment: we applied the time-based split Marcus proposed: 65% Redwood responsibility, 35% third-party. Based on Skyline’s impacted request volume and contract tier, that yields a provisional credit equal to 0.65 * (pro-rated outage minutes) applied against November invoice. We’ll finalize the credit after legal signs off; expect a confirmation email and credit memo within 10 business days.

- Exclusion denial: we cannot accept a full third-party exclusion for the whole impacted interval because the evidence shows internal degradation outside the ProxyNet resets. We did, however, reduce our total counted outage accordingly.

Action items:
- Redwood (Marissa/Neha): produce a formal credit memo and update the invoice.
- Skyline (Theo): confirm acceptance of the provisional apportionment so we can close the ticket; if you’d prefer a dispute, we’ll route to legal ops.
- EdgeProxy: thanks for providing ProxyNet’s bulletin; if you have additional logs linking the resets to specific backhaul hops, forward them to proxy-ops@redwood.com.

Internal reference: INC-20261129-85 (shared link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/INC-20261129-85).

— Irene
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
